[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for fantasy football draft preparation include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Know your league settings: Understand the scoring system, roster size, and position requirements.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Rank players: Create a cheat sheet with top players at each position, considering past performance, team changes, and injuries.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Identify sleepers and breakout candidates: Look for players who might exceed expectations.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Focus on consistent performers: Players with a consistent track record are often more reliable.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Pay attention to ADP (Average Draft Position): Know when players are typically drafted.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Develop a draft strategy: Decide on RB-heavy, WR-heavy, or balanced approach.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 7. Prepare for your draft position: Focus on top-tier players if picking early, look for value picks if picking later.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 8. Mock drafts: Participate in mock drafts to practice strategy.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 9. Stay up-to-date on preseason news: Monitor injuries and training camp performances.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 10. Have a draft-day plan: Bring cheat sheet, rankings, and potential picks to the draft.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Prioritizing players on the cheat sheet involves considering a mix of factors for each position:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] For Quarterbacks (QBs): Past performance, team changes, strength of schedule, rushing ability.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] For Running Backs (RBs): Workload, efficiency, team's rushing philosophy, injury history.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] For Wide Receivers (WRs): Target share, yardage and touchdowns, quarterback play, team's passing philosophy.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] For Tight Ends (TEs): Target share, quarterback play, red-zone usage, blocking ability.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] For Kickers (Ks): Team's scoring offense, field goal accuracy, extra point attempts, strength of schedule.
